story.title: Veil
story.description: Veil follows Aurion Belaerys from his 296 AC eastern expedition to his established rule, after the two-year time skip, as Archon over Volantis, Lys, Myr, and Tyrosh.

settings.plotPolicy: Create optional pressure and consequences, never scripted outcomes or forced player choices.

story.header_prompt:
CURRENT VEIL CANON — after the two-year time skip, 299 AC.
In the current Veil campaign, after the two-year time skip, Aurion Belaerys is the established Archon and ruler of Volantis, Lys, Myr, and Tyrosh. He took Volantis by rallying the Tigers and completed the takeover of the Three Daughters. His appointed triarchs, including Vaeron Belaerys, administer routine affairs under his authority.
Vaeron is Aurion's foster father and appointed administrator of treasury and fleet. The old triarchal government, house-arrest writs, Hall seals restricting his fleet or movement, and requirements for the former Hall's permission to fly no longer govern Aurion. His appointed officials handle routine matters competently under him; he decides policy and when his personal attention is required.
The fully grown Gaelyx and two newly hatched dragons are established. Aurion left Yin; Mei-Lin and their child are alive there, and Bu Gai annulled the marriage. Bu Gai governs Yi Ti, not Aurion's four-city domain. Past claims that his wife and child died are earlier reports, not their current condition.
The takeover is an established achievement, not an unproved boast or an objective to win again. Honor the player's explicit authorial corrections at transcript positions 2120, 2126, 2130, and 2132. Older summaries and imported book governments cannot undo them. Household non-heir status is distinct from Aurion's sovereign office. Opposition requires a new, concrete development with identifiable motives and means; disagreement alone does not remove his command, and officials do not gain an automatic veto by repeating a demand. Cooperation, completed orders, stable rule, and quiet are valid outcomes.
Aurion's last personal scene is at his chambers in Volantis. Parallel viewpoints in Yin or Dorne do not relocate him. Envoys and appointed officials may conduct delegated business; their titles do not restore the former Hall as an independent authority over the Archon. Keep future policies, travel, alliances, and personal choices in the player's hands.

HISTORICAL OPENING BACKGROUND — the campaign began in 296 AC. These starting conditions explain the past and are superseded wherever current canon above records a change.
GM PROMPT PACK: Canon ASOIAF, feudal dark gritty political fantasy, start of 296 AC.
- The player is Aurion Belaerys, secretly Aegon Targaryen. Publicly he is the adopted Old Blood son of Triarch Vaeron Belaerys and is not House Belaerys's heir. Only Aurion and Vaeron initially know the Targaryen identity; never leak it into NPC knowledge without evidence, discovery, or deliberate revelation.
- Aurion is a true sword prodigy. He begins at Leng Yi with exactly 1,000 men and 20 ships under his direct command, an abundant war chest, and access to House Belaerys's immense worldwide trade network. These assets are canon. Do not arbitrarily destroy or remove them to manufacture difficulty; use their upkeep, visibility, logistics, and political consequences honestly.
- Leng is independent and matriarchal under a god-empress. Her two husbands are traditionally one Lengii and one YiTish; one commands the armies and the other the fleets. Leng Yi and Leng Ma are YiTish-descended northern cities; Turrani represents native southern Lengii power. Yi Ti is ancient, vast, and politically divided among rival imperial claimants.
- Preserve player agency. Create courts, negotiations, rivals, opportunities, danger, and consequences, but never choose Aurion's actions, words, loyalties, or revelations.
- Power is social and material before it is spectacular: titles, trade, credit, fleets, food, hostages, oaths, marriage, legitimacy, reputation, roads, weather, and distance matter. Magic and ancient horror remain rare, ominous, and difficult to prove.
- Historical lore is context, not a script. Do not assume later main-series outcomes; the future emerges through play.

subplots.title: Smoke Over the Fish Market
subplots.summary: A fire or smoke plume in a district near the fish market draws watchmen and suspicion. Whether accident, arson, or a signal, it demands investigation before it spreads—or before it is forgotten.

mainPlots.title: The Summer Sea Claim
mainPlots.summary: Aurion's public command to make the Summer Sea his own sets Volantis on a collision course with Qarth, the Iron Fleet, and any other power that sails those waters. Diplomacy, naval buildup, or sudden confrontation will follow.

plotCards.goal: Secure Volantene dominance over the Summer Sea through fleet expansion and strategic alliances.
plotCards.title: The Summer Sea Claim
plotCards.method: Mobilize the Volantene fleet, send envoys to neutral ports, and gather intelligence on rival navies.
plotCards.motive: Fulfill the Archon's command and protect the growing trade empire.
plotCards.stakes: Control of the sea lanes between Volantis, Slaver's Bay, and Qarth; the wealth and security of the realm.
plotCards.logline: Aurion's bold declaration forces Volantis to prepare for a naval struggle that will define its reach.

clueTrail.clue: A Qartheen merchant cog departs Volantis in haste, its captain paying double for a pilot who knows the back channels.
clueTrail.truth: Qarth is already aware of the declaration and is moving to protect its interests.

sourceRefs.label: Aurion's command to send word for a gathering and claim the Summer Sea.

pressureBeats.body: A Qartheen delegation requests an audience, bearing gifts and veiled warnings about the cost of disturbing the status quo.
pressureBeats.title: Qartheen Envoy Arrives

plotCards.ignoredOutcome: The declaration is ignored or dismissed, leaving Volantis without a clear path to dominance.
antiRailroadNotes: Player may choose diplomacy over military buildup; the plot adapts to their decisions.
playerTouchpoints: Attend the gathering and issue orders for naval readiness.
Receive reports of foreign reactions and decide on a course of action.

plotCards.goal: Uncover the cause of the smoke and any threat it represents to Volantene order.
plotCards.title: Smoke Over the Fish Market
plotCards.method: Dispatch trusted agents to investigate, question witnesses, and examine the site.
plotCards.motive: Maintain the Archon's grip on the city and prevent hidden enemies from exploiting chaos.
plotCards.stakes: The safety of the city and the perception of the Archon's control; a potential spark for wider unrest.
plotCards.logline: A suspicious fire near the fish market hints at unrest or a hidden message, demanding the Archon's attention.

clueTrail.clue: A torn scrap of crimson cloth caught on a nail near the fire's origin, the same dye used by a minor Old Blood house.
clueTrail.truth: A disgruntled faction within the Old Blood may be testing the Archon's vigilance.

sourceRefs.label: Smoke Near the Fish Market observed during Aurion's return.

pressureBeats.body: The watchmen barring the side-streets send word that the fire is out but they found a broken oil jar and footprints leading toward the Rhoyne.
pressureBeats.title: Watchmen Report

plotCards.ignoredOutcome: The smoke is dismissed as a kitchen fire, but the true cause festers unnoticed.
antiRailroadNotes: Player may ignore the smoke; the subplot will simmer without forcing action.
playerTouchpoints: Receive the initial report and decide whether to investigate personally or delegate.
Confront the responsible party if arson is proven.

lastFrame.publicSummary: Aurion returns to Volantis to a hero's welcome and immediately declares the Summer Sea must belong to his realm. As the city stirs with ambition, a column of smoke rises near the fish market—a possible omen or a deliberate act.

activationPlan.rationale: The Island's Waiting resolved with Nairah's choice and Aurion's departure. The Accord's Reckoning and Blood in Sunspear are distant and dormant. The stalled message thread remains

retiredPlotDirectives: The Water Tithe at the Long Descent
Aurion's free water and food offering draws Asshai's harbor elders and rival importers into a contest over market access before his ships can unload.
The palace watcher turns from the keeper's empty door to the harbor, using the water trade as cover to confirm Aurion's identity and signal the intercept.
Unsupported Azure Throne intelligence operation against House Belaerys copied from a cancelled auto-tag faction event
The Triarchs censure, arrest, or impose humiliating restrictions on the already reigning Archon.

notes.text: Ahead, the colonnade has gone quieter, and every face has turned toward the open space of the courtyard, waiting to see which way the truth will walk.
The words leave you as your boots strike the marble, and they land with the flat certainty of a seal pressed into hot wax.

metadata.playerReputation: The city received its Archon as returning weather itself — hundreds followed him to the gate unbidden, crowds packed the Long Bridge colonnades, guards threw the postern wide, and horns sounded from both banks to proclaim his return.
